turn_text: Things are going well from that standpoint. I had respect on both sides of the aisle and I get things done. I'm a very moderate person and I'm not here to throw a lot of elbows in my opponent, but my opponent really has shown all the signs that she's going to be more of a partisan, more of a far-left member of Congress if she gets elected. And that's just not where I am. That's not my zip code. My friend is not my DNA.

The speaker’s personal identity aligns with mainstream centrism.
The speaker’s credibility depends on contrasting themselves with their opponent.
Respect across party lines indicates legitimacy and competence.
Audience members will recognize 'zip code' as a metaphor for ideological alignment.
Political opponents who prioritize conflict are less trustworthy.
Ideological distance correlates with policy divergence and risk.
